title: Drop `volatile` on ordinary guest loads/stores; add explicit barriers only where the guest needs them
evidence: out/ppc_tu4/ppc_context.h:46 `#define PPC_LOAD_U32(x) __builtin_bswap32(*(volatile uint32_t*)(base + (x)))`, :82 same for stores. Asm of sub_826214E8 (an 8-iteration ld/std copy loop, extracted to scratchpad t1.cpp): with volatile, each iteration does `mov [rdi+80],rcx` / `mov rcx,[rdi+72]` / `add rcx,8` / `mov [rdi+72],rcx` / `mov edx,[rdi+64]` / `add qword [rdi+64],8`, i.e. ctx.r8/r9/r10 are reloaded and re-stored every access. With `volatile ` stripped from a copy of ppc_context.h: 756 -> 631 asm lines, 647 -> 516 instructions (-20%), and ctx-relative memory operands roughly 228 -> 123 (approximate grep). sub_82263C28 (454 lines, r14-r31 heavy): 581 -> 513 instructions (-12%). LLVM's AA treats volatile as ModRef against everything, so the `__restrict ctx` has no effect. Hazard counts in out/ppc_tu4 (loops.py): 17,317 backward gotos, of which 2,458 are loops with PPC_LOAD but no store, call, CAS or fence; those are potential poll loops that LICM would turn into an infinite loop. sync 11, lwsync 2, eieio 13 sites. Existing mmioStore() split in recompiler.cpp (~1521 on) already identifies MMIO stores.
proposal: In XenonUtils/ppc_context.h define PPC_LOAD_*/PPC_STORE_* as plain accesses. Keep volatile only for PPC_MM_STORE_* and the lwarx/stwcx paths (recompiler.cpp ~1065, ~1211, ~1550, ~1706). In recompiler.cpp: (1) emit `asm volatile("":::"memory")` for sync/lwsync/eieio/isync; (2) in the per-function CFG, find natural loops with no store, call, or CAS and that contain a load. Emit a compiler barrier on their back-edge. To narrow it further, a loop needs the barrier only if no register written inside the loop reaches the exit condition (pure spin on an unchanged address register); that is the cheap dataflow check. (3) Keep volatile on loads of the 13+11+2 fenced regions if some guest code does double-reads across a sync. Validate by diffing a 60 s bench plus a replay checksum.
expected_gain: Estimate: 12-20% fewer host instructions in recompiled code, measured on two sample functions; on a CPU-bound weak machine (FX-8350, 5800H iGPU) maybe 5-10% of t3/CP-adjacent guest time. Arithmetic: 581->513 = -11.7%, 647->516 = -20.2%, weighted by the fraction of runtime spent in guest code (unknown, likely 30-50% on the FX). Zero gain on GPU-bound desktop PCs.
risk: Medium-high. Missed poll loops hang at runtime, so the loop analysis must be conservative (2,458 sites get a barrier, 14% of back-edges). Compiler may merge two reads of the same guest word within a function (races with other host threads). The MMIO/GPU-ring write ordering must stay volatile. Needs a gate: run FM2 under the full autoplay path on the FX before shipping.

verify.evidence_checked:
I confirmed the static numbers. ppc_context.h:46 and :82 define PPC_LOAD_U32 and PPC_STORE_U32 as volatile accesses, and PPC_FUNC takes `ctx` as `__restrict` (line 30). The build uses -fno-strict-aliasing (CMakeLists.txt:32), and the researcher's cc.sh and ccnv.sh use the same flags (-O2 -msse4.1 -fno-strict-aliasing). From the researcher's existing asm files I counted 647 -> 516 instructions for sub_826214E8 (-20%) and 581 -> 513 for the second sample (-12%). Memory-operand greps gave 231 -> 130 for the first function and 228 -> 184 for the second, so the "228 -> 123" claim was only roughly right for the second function. I did not recompile.

Problems with the finding:
1. The loop-hazard filter is incomplete. It counts only loops with a load and no store, call, CAS or fence. A poll loop with a timeout counter, such as `while (*flag == 0 && --n)`, writes only ctx registers, which count as stores in that filter. With `__restrict ctx`, LLVM may assume those ctx stores do not alias the guest load, so it can hoist the load and make the loop spin forever. The 2,458 figure therefore undercounts the loops that need a barrier, and the proposed "no register written reaches the exit" refinement would remove some barriers the analysis actually needs.
2. Stores lose x86 ordering. Non-volatile guest stores can be merged, sunk, dead-store-eliminated or reordered with each other. Guest lock-free code that relies on store order without a sync gets no protection. Only sync, lwsync and eieio would carry barriers, and PPC_MM_STORE_* is currently #define'd to PPC_STORE_*, so it would silently lose volatile unless it is split out.
3. Guest memory is shared with host threads, including the GPU command-processor thread and the XMA/APU threads. Compiler merging of repeated loads can race with them.

Not shown: any runtime or fps measurement. The gain is static instruction count only. The finding itself says guest code is unmeasured, 30-50% of runtime on the FX. This also overlaps the already-parked "volatile blocks register caching" item, with no new evidence that overcomes its hang-risk blocker beyond the proposed loop analysis, which is flawed as above.
verify.corrected_gain: Static: about -12% to -20% host instructions on two sample functions (reproduced from the researcher's asm, not recompiled). Runtime gain is unmeasured. Treat it as an estimate of a few percent of guest-code time on the FX (12-20% fewer instructions times a 30-50% guest share = 4-10%), and roughly zero on GPU-bound PCs. Fewer instructions does not mean the same fraction less time.
verify.blockers: The loop-barrier analysis must also treat loops that write only ctx registers, such as counters, as poll-loop candidates, so the real barrier count is above 2,458. The proposal does not address store reordering, merging and elimination without sync. PPC_MM_STORE_* must be given its own volatile definition. Any version should be gated by an A/B test of the whole recompiled game on the FX before shipping, because a missed poll loop shows up as a hang. A cheaper, safer first step is to measure a whole-TU build with volatile stripped for fps on the FX, with the barrier work deferred until that shows a gain.

title: Make r14-r31 (and f14-f31, v14-v31, v64-v127) locals safe via a read-before-write dataflow pass, with inline save/restore helpers
evidence: Only 109 of 50,530 functions (0.2%) read a callee-saved GPR before writing it (funclet.py, linear-order approximation treating __savegprlr/stw-to-r1 prologue saves as transparent). Examples: sub_82773570 reads r14-r31, sub_827743C8 reads r30, sub_82775EC8 reads r28, sub_827861F0 reads r24. sub_82773570 has no direct callers (grep: only its definition at ppc_recomp.101.cpp:15263), so it is entered indirectly, from a table/host. Save/restore helper call sites that would need inlining: __savegprlr 11,536, __restgprlr 12,794, __savefpr 340, __restfpr 358, __savevmx/restvmx 44 each (24,330 helper calls). Experiment on sub_82263C28: textually replacing ctx.r14..r31 with locals (ignoring helper semantics) takes it 581 -> 527 instructions (-9.3%) with volatile, 513 -> 517 without volatile (the two wins overlap a lot in this function). Upstream config exists (non_volatile_as_local, recompiler.cpp:271-296 and :391) but only handles __save/__rest by name, with no analysis for readers such as funclets.
proposal: ReXenon (XenonRecomp/recompiler.cpp, on the existing per-function CFG): (1) per function compute LIVEIN_nv = r14-r31 read before written on some path, treating the __savegprlr_N / stw rN,off(r1) pattern and the matching restores as transparent, because they only preserve the caller's values. Base it on D:\fm2-decomp\tools\decomp\livein.py, which already does this iterative whole-program liveness for r3-r10/f1-f13. (2) Propagate transitively: a function NEEDY if LIVEIN_nv is non-empty or it tail-calls (`b` outside the function) a NEEDY function. (3) At every call site (bl/bctrl) to a NEEDY target, and at every bctrl/indirect call whose target is not known to be non-needy, emit `ctx.rN = rN` for the dirty locals in LIVEIN_nv(callee), or all dirty locals for unknown targets. Functions with no direct callers or in the hooked list (ppc_hooks.h, setjmp/longjmp paths in Lua) get r14-r31 locals disabled or spill-on-entry. (4) Emit the save/rest helpers inline on the locals (stw/std/lfd/stvx to the r1 slot, ld back into the local), which also drops the 24,330 helper calls and their ctx.r12/ctx.lr stores. (5) Exclude any function the SEH-funclet detector or the hook list flags. Verify with the existing coverage harness by diffing ctx.r14-31 at every function exit.
expected_gain: Estimate: -9% host instructions on sub_82263C28 as one data point; inlining 24,330 helper calls removes ~2 call/ret + 2 ctx stores each. Gain on guest CPU time maybe 3-8% alone, less when combined with finding 1 (the two overlap: 513 vs 517 instructions in the sample). Only matters on CPU-bound machines.
risk: Medium. Any missed reader of the parent's nonvolatile registers (funclet, longjmp/Lua, exception handler, hooks reading ctx.rN) silently corrupts state; the 109-function set must be computed from the real CFG, not my linear approximation (which may miss a few, e.g. it did not list sub_8242A6DC/sub_824328FC named earlier). Hooks in src/ read ctx.r* at function entry/exit, so hooked functions must keep ctx-resident registers.

verify.evidence_checked:
Reproduced: ran funclet.py over out/ppc_tu4 and got 50,530 functions, 109 with a read-before-write of r14-r31. That set includes sub_82773570, sub_8242A6DC [r22,r27] and sub_824328FC [r27], so the finding's risk note that the script "did not list" the last two is wrong. sub_82773570 has only its definition and the func_mapping entry, so it is entered indirectly.

Checked in source: recompiler.cpp:268-296 and :391 are the upstream nonVolatileRegistersAsLocalVariables handling. It prints nothing for __save*/__rest* helpers and has no readers analysis. fm2_tu4.toml:20 has non_volatile_as_local = false. PPC_LOAD/STORE are volatile in ppc_context.h (lines 38-74), so the premise holds. sub_8242A6DC reads r22 and r27, and r27 is the parent's value used as a frame pointer, after storing the callee-saves. That confirms the funclet hazard, and it is exactly the parked blocker.

Instruction counts from the researcher's own asm files, which I counted with a crude grep and did not recompile: t1 647->516, t2 581->513 (these two are the 20%/12% locals-only versions), t2l 527->517. These are static line counts only. Nothing was timed.

Gaps:
1. The 109-function set is a linear approximation and the proposal says to recompute it on the real CFG.
2. The finding covers readers of the parent's registers but not writers. Guest longjmp and any context-restore path write ctx.r14-r31 and then return into a caller whose locals are now stale. Lua uses setjmp/longjmp. After any call that can write r14-r31, such as setjmp and its longjmp return, the caller would have to reload its locals. The proposal does not mention this.
3. Dropping the save stores means the r1 save slots are no longer written. Anything that reads those slots, such as an unwinder or SEH, would see stale data.
4. Hooks in src/ read ctx.r22-r31 (perf_probe.cpp:316-378), so hooked functions need exemption. The proposal already says this.
5. The expected gain is an estimate. The 3-8% guest-CPU figure has no arithmetic behind it and no timing. Earlier work in this project found t3 is not the fps limit on fast PCs, and on the FX the dominant costs were the ring memcpy and the fetch table. So the gain is real only on CPU-bound machines.
verify.corrected_gain: Static host instruction reduction of roughly 2% to 20% on the sampled functions (the t2l sample, where volatile is the only difference, shows just 527->517). That is not translated to runtime. Treat the 3-8% CPU-time gain as an unmeasured guess, and only on CPU-bound machines such as the FX and iGPU laptops. Needs a timing A/B on the FX, which this research cannot do.
verify.blockers: The funclet blocker is solvable in principle (a read-before-write pass plus flushing before calls to needy functions), but the finding does not cover writers. Setjmp/longjmp and other context-restoring guest code write ctx.r14-r31 behind the caller's back, so after calls to such functions the caller must reload its locals. Indirect calls (bctrl) to unknown targets need conservative flush and reload on both sides, which cuts into the gain. The hooks list must be excluded. The 109 count needs recomputing on the real CFG. Effort is L with silent-corruption risk, and verification needs a ctx.r14-31 diff harness at every function exit.

title: FCTID/FCTIDZ of exactly 2^63 returns 0x8000000000000000 instead of saturating to LLONG_MAX
evidence: recompiler.cpp:910-916: `({}.f64 > double(LLONG_MAX)) ? LLONG_MAX : simde_mm_cvtsd_si64(...)`. double(LLONG_MAX) rounds up to exactly 2^63, so the `>` test is false for 2^63 itself and x86 cvtsd2si returns the indefinite value 0x8000... (LLONG_MIN). PPC saturates to 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF. FCTIWZ (line ~921) is fine because INT_MAX is exactly representable.
proposal: Change `>` to `>=` in the FCTID and FCTIDZ templates (comparison against 2^63). Optionally add a unit test emitting FCTID for 2^63, 2^63-1024, NaN (expect 0x8000...), and -2^63-2048.
expected_gain: Correctness only: fixes the value for any double >= 2^63 and < +inf-class edge. Rarely hit; the NaN case already matches (0x8000...). Zero perf cost.
risk: Very low.

verify.evidence_checked: Re-read D:\ReXenon\XenonRecomp\recompiler.cpp lines 912-920. FCTID (line 914) and FCTIDZ (line 919) both emit `(f64 > double(LLONG_MAX)) ? LLONG_MAX : simde_mm_cvt(t)sd_si64(...)`. double(LLONG_MAX) rounds to exactly 2^63. The `>` test is therefore false for an input of exactly 2^63. x86 cvtsd2si/cvttsd2si then returns the indefinite value 0x8000000000000000, but PPC saturates to 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF. I did not compile and run the case; this follows from the code and from x86 and PPC semantics. +inf takes the `>` branch and is correct. NaN and anything below -2^63 give 0x8000... on both architectures, so those match. FCTIWZ (line 924) is unaffected because INT_MAX is exactly representable. Generated code in out\ppc_tu4 uses the same pattern, for example `ctx.f0.s64 = (ctx.f0.f64 > double(LLONG_MAX)) ? LLONG_MAX : simde_mm_cvttsd_si64(...)`. Counts across the 204 files: 652 lines contain `double(LLONG_MAX)` (FCTID plus FCTIDZ sites) and 13 lines contain `cvtsd_si64`. I did not split the 652 by instruction. The `>` to `>=` change is semantically safe. It does not affect SEH funclets, threads or MMIO, and costs essentially nothing. The only real limit on the gain is how rarely a game feeds exactly 2^63 to a convert.
verify.corrected_gain: Correctness only, with zero performance change. It applies to 652 generated sites in FM2 tu4 (FCTID and FCTIDZ combined), but only an input of exactly 2^63 triggers the wrong result. Any double above 2^63 is already caught by `>`. The practical impact is very low, but it is a real, exact bug and a trivial two-character fix on lines 914 and 919. Since `>=` also gets all values at or above 2^63 right, the guard could become `>= 9223372036854775808.0` for clarity.
verify.blockers: None. Not proven to be hit by FM2 or PGR4 at runtime. Recompiled output must be regenerated for the fix to reach the games. Could not diff PGR4's patched copy, which may already carry this fix.

title: Skip the `ctx.lr = ...` store when the callee provably never reads LR (whole-program mflr analysis)
evidence: 216,290 `ctx.lr = 0x...` stores in out/ppc_tu4 (grep); 40,913 `= ctx.lr` reads (mflr) and 29,563 `ctx.lr = ctx.r12` (mtlr). lr.py over 50,729 functions: 45,559 need LR (read it, or tail-call something that does or an indirect target); 148,982 bl sites, of which 37,065 (24.9%) call a function that never reads LR on any path (neither itself nor via tail-calls). 21,915 bctrl sites must keep the store (unknown target). Each store is `mov eax, imm32; mov [rcx+256], rax`, 2 instructions (see asm above for __savegprlr_29 call setup).
proposal: In recompiler.cpp PPC_INST_BL (~706): consult a per-target 'readsLr' bit computed in the analysis pass (fixed point over tail-call edges); emit the store only when the bit is set, the target is unknown/hooked, or the target is in the hook table (src/hooks, 305 ctx.lr references in src/ must be checked first; the toml notes Lua setjmp/longjmp and diagnostics read LR from ctx).
expected_gain: Estimate: 37,065 of ~216,290 stores removed (17% of LR stores) = ~74k instructions out of the whole program, mostly outside hot loops; likely under 1% runtime. Low value alone, but it is a code-size/i-cache win and a prerequisite for the inline helper work in finding 2.
risk: Low-medium: diagnostics/stack walkers and Lua longjmp read ctx.lr, so those paths must be audited or the analysis must treat hooked targets as readers.

verify.evidence_checked: Re-ran the greps in out/ppc_tu4. 216,290 "ctx.lr = " stores reproduced exactly. Of those, 29,563 are mtlr ("ctx.lr = ctx.r12") and about 186.7k are call-site stores ("ctx.lr = 0x", 186,717), so the "216,290 call-site stores" framing mixes in mtlr. 40,913 "= ctx.lr" reads reproduced. PPC_CALL_INDIRECT_FUNC appears in 22,473 lines (about 21.9k bctrl plus tail-call indirects), which is consistent with the 21,915 bctrl figure. recompiler.cpp:706-707 (BL) emits the store unconditionally unless config.skipLr, and lines 647 (BCTRL) and 726 match the description. The analysis logic in lr.py is sound: a function needs LR if it contains an mflr, makes an indirect tail call, or tail-calls a function that needs LR. I did not rerun lr.py or reproduce the 37,065 figure. Not verified: src has 305 ctx.lr references (for example fibers.cpp and crash.cpp print ctx.lr in diagnostics), and the analysis must treat hooked or imported targets as readers. That audit is not yet done and is an unverified risk. No host assembly was produced, so the store cost (2 instructions) is unmeasured.
verify.corrected_gain: Overstated or at best unmeasured. About 37k of roughly 186.7k call-site stores (not 216k) would go, which is about 74k instructions across the whole program, mostly cold. Expected runtime gain is well under 1% and likely unmeasurable. On a weak CPU such as the FX it may reach a few tenths of a percent, plus a small code-size benefit. Treat it as a low-priority cleanup, not a speed win.
verify.blockers: The counts reproduce, but the gain is negligible and the change carries semantic risk. The hook table, the fiber and crash diagnostics, and Lua setjmp/longjmp handling all read ctx.lr, so any hooked or imported callee would need to be treated as a reader. Whole-program analysis would also have to be rerun whenever the config or hooks change. Not worth doing unless it is bundled with other inline-helper work.

title: Drop volatile on guest loads/stores; keep it only for loads in call-free loops
evidence: ppc_context.h:37-87 all PPC_LOAD_*/PPC_STORE_* are volatile. Generated counts (grep in out/ppc_tu4): LOAD U8/16/32/64 = 16032/4047/278633/27256, STORE = 13935/3666/192804/24886. A/B compile with clang-cl /O2 /Ob2 -msse4.1, same flags as build/tu/build.ninja, non-volatile macros force-included from nv.h. ppc_recomp.101.cpp: instructions 26304 -> 25218 (-4.1%), host loads 4400 -> 3716 (-15.5%), stores 7055 -> 6618 (-6%), bswaps 1802 -> 1703, obj 227352 -> 222974 bytes. ppc_recomp.50.cpp: 39435 -> 36301 instr (-7.9%), loads 7135 -> 5663 (-20.6%), stores 9317 -> 8226 (-12%), obj 292003 -> 280342. Per-function diffs: 197 functions smaller, 13 larger of 256 in file 50. Example: __imp__sub_82484060 shrinks 193 -> 92 instructions because its 35-iteration stb loop (out/ppc_tu4/ppc_recomp.50.cpp, loc_8248409C) becomes a memset; volatile forbids idiom recognition, merging, store-to-load forwarding and dead-store elimination. Hazard check: a non-volatile polling loop (spin.cpp in scratch) compiles to a bare 'ret' (loop deleted), the volatile version keeps the 'mov/test/je' loop, so a blanket removal would hang spin-waits. Loop census (census.py over all 204 files, 50,966 functions): 17,317 backward gotos; 7,616 whose label..goto range has no call (no 'ctx, base);', PPC_CALL_INDIRECT_FUNC or 'ctx.lr ='); 3,462 of those have no store either. Loads inside call-free loop ranges = 20,138 (6.2% of 325,968); inside call-free store-free (pure poll) loops = 4,460 (1.4%). Loads inside any loop = 75,003 (23%).
proposal: In recompiler.cpp, before emitting a function, prescan its instruction list: for every branch with target address T <= branch address B, mark [T,B]; if no bl/bctrl/blrl falls in [T,B] mark it spin-capable. Emit PPC_LOAD_*_V (volatile, current macros) for loads inside marked ranges and plain PPC_LOAD_* (non-volatile, still bswap) elsewhere. Stores can be non-volatile everywhere once barriers (next finding) exist. Safety argument: every call goes through sub_X, which is PPC_WEAK_FUNC noinline (ppc_context.h:33), so it cannot be inlined or hoisted across, and calls stay opaque for memory. Cheaper tier first: volatile only for the 3,462 call-free store-free loops (1.4% of loads); a second tier of all call-free loops costs 6.2%. Keep volatile in host-side macros for MMIO. Validate by rebuilding one TU and running the A/B tour.
expected_gain: Estimate: 3-6% fewer host instructions in recompiled code overall (two sampled files -4.1% and -7.9%, minus the ~6% of loads left volatile, so likely ~3-6%). Dynamic gain is unmeasured, so treat it as 2-5% of recompiled-code CPU time. That only shows on CPU-bound machines (FX-8350, 5800H iGPU), not on the GPU-CP-bound 5800X. Also enables memset/memcpy idiom recognition for copy loops.
risk: Hangs if a polling loop is missed (the spin.cpp test shows the loop is deleted); loops entered via computed jumps or interleaved with host-visible effects are not covered by the range heuristic. Needs the barrier finding first. Needs a Dekker-free review of the 11 sync sites. Possible compiler memcpy/vectorisation of byte loops touching GPU/write-combined memory (should be fine on host RAM views). A mismatched-width overlap pattern in guest byte-copy loops is handled by LLVM's alias checks, but test.

verify.evidence_checked:
Reproduced the A/B. I compiled ppc_recomp.101.cpp with the build.ninja flags (/O2 /Ob2 -msse4.1 -fno-strict-aliasing), once as-is and once with a force-included non-volatile macro header. The object sizes came out at 227352 and 222974 bytes, exactly the claimed numbers. Instruction lines in the .s output fell 24368 -> 23201 (-4.8% on my crude grep), and bswaps 1802 -> 1703, matching the claim. I did not re-run file 50 or the function-level diffs. I did not re-run the loop census or the per-kind load/store counts; the 6.2% and 1.4% shares are unverified.

Source checks:
- ppc_context.h:37-87 confirms every load and store macro is volatile, and PPC_WEAK_FUNC at line 33 is weak+noinline, so calls are opaque.
- recompiler.cpp:1239 (LWSYNC) and 1758 (SYNC) are both "no op" and emit nothing. There is currently no compiler barrier anywhere except __sync_bool_compare_and_swap for stwcx/stdcx (691 sites in out/ppc_tu4).
- lwarx is a plain load, and the CAS is only a barrier for that stwcx.

Soundness gaps:
- Today volatile is the only thing ordering guest memory ops against each other. The proposal's "stores non-volatile everywhere" is only valid once barriers are emitted for sync, lwsync, eieio and isync. isync matters because acquire idioms (load, compare, branch, isync) would otherwise let later loads be hoisted. That is a prerequisite change, not a small tweak.
- The loop prescan relies on backward direct branches. Loops closed through bctr switch tables or computed gotos are not covered. A missed poll loop hangs, and the spin.cpp test shows the loop is deleted.
- Dynamic gain is entirely unmeasured. Static instruction shrink is not runtime gain. On FX/5800H CPU-bound machines it would plausibly be low single digits. On a GPU-CP-bound 5800X it is invisible.
verify.corrected_gain: Static host-instruction reduction of about -4% in file 101 (reproduced) and -8% in file 50 (claimed, not re-run). Expect maybe 1-4% of recompiled-code CPU time on CPU-bound machines only, still an estimate. Roughly 0% where the GPU CP thread is the limit.
verify.blockers:
1. Real compiler barriers must be emitted first for sync, lwsync, eieio and isync (currently all no-ops).
2. The poll-loop detector must cover computed-jump and switch-table loops, or fall back to volatile for any function containing bctr.
3. Dynamic payoff has to be measured on the FX before committing.
4. Hang risk is silent: a missed poll loop is compiled away entirely, so it needs a regression test.

title: sync/lwsync/eieio/isync emit nothing: add compiler barriers (and mfence for sync)
evidence: recompiler.cpp:865-867 EIEIO '// no op', :1239-1241 LWSYNC '// no op', :1758-1760 SYNC '// no op'. Sites in out/ppc_tu4: sync 11, eieio 13, lwsync 2, isync 0 (about 26 total). Xenia emits f.MemoryBarrier() for eieio and sync (ppc_emit_memory.cc:846-854, a full mfence), and isync is a Nop. Today volatile accidentally orders volatile accesses against each other, but not against non-volatile accesses (lvx/stvx via simde loads, memset from dcbz, CAS), and x86 hardware still reorders store->load, which sync exists to prevent.
proposal: In recompiler.cpp emit: SYNC -> __atomic_thread_fence(__ATOMIC_SEQ_CST) (mfence, 11 sites); LWSYNC and EIEIO -> asm volatile("" ::: "memory") (x86 TSO already gives store-store/load-load/load-store order, so only compiler ordering is needed; Xenia uses full barrier for eieio, use mfence there if a GPU ring test shows a need); ISYNC -> compiler barrier. Define them as PPC_SYNC()/PPC_LWSYNC()/PPC_EIEIO() macros in ppc_context.h so an aarch64 host (ppc_context.h already has mrs fpcr code) can map to dmb ish / dmb ishst. This is the prerequisite for dropping volatile.
expected_gain: No speed change (about 26 static sites). Removes a latent store->load ordering bug (Dekker/Peterson style handshakes through sync) and makes the memory-model contract explicit.
risk: A compiler 'memory' clobber forces ctx fields to be written back and reloaded around the barrier; only 26 sites, negligible. mfence costs about 30-100 cycles per execution; the 11 sync sites should not be hot (not measured).

verify.evidence_checked:
Re-checked the source. EIEIO, LWSYNC and SYNC are empty cases ("no op") in D:\ReXenon\XenonRecomp\recompiler.cpp at about lines 865, 1239 and 1758, matching the claim. ppc_context.h defines every guest load and store as a volatile access. The compiler therefore keeps them in order relative to each other, but x86 can still reorder a store ahead of a later load, which is what sync prevents. lwarx/stwcx is emitted as __sync_bool_compare_and_swap (ppc_recomp.1.cpp line 8214 and others), a full barrier on x86, so those sites are already ordered.

I could not confirm the site counts (sync 11, eieio 13, lwsync 2). The recompiler emits nothing for these instructions, so grep on out\ppc_tu4 cannot find them. My grep for "sync" only hit the CAS builtin. The counts must have come from the disassembly or the instruction stream, and I did not reproduce them. I did not compile anything and did not measure mfence cost. I did not open the Xenia source to re-check the claim about its full barrier.

The change is semantically safe. A compiler barrier or mfence at about 26 sites cannot break SEH funclets, polling loops or MMIO, and nothing in the parked list conflicts with it.
verify.corrected_gain: No speed gain. This is a small, latent correctness and memory-model hardening change. The 26-site count is unverified. title: stwcx./stdcx. emulation is a value-compare CAS: no ABA protection, no reservation-address check
evidence: recompiler.cpp:1703-1711 (STWCX) and :1547-1555 (STDCX): cr0.eq = __sync_bool_compare_and_swap(base+ea, reserved, bswap(rS)); LWARX at :1210-1216 and LDARX :1064-1070 only stash the raw loaded value in 'reserved' (a local with PPC_CONFIG_RESERVED_AS_LOCAL, out/ppc_tu4/ppc_config.h). If a second core does A->B->A between lwarx and stwcx. the CAS succeeds where real hardware reservation (a 128-byte granule, killed by any store) fails. It also succeeds if there was no lwarx at all and the memory happens to equal the stale 'reserved', and when lwarx/stwcx addresses differ but values match. Xenia (backend/x64/x64_backend.cc:1555-1700) keeps per-thread reserve_address + generation snapshot, checks the address, and uses a 1M-entry per-granule generation table bumped on each successful stwcx. FM2 census (c2.py over all generated cpp): 672+3 lwarx/ldarx, 686+5 stwcx/stdcx; all 691 pairs are in the same function with identical (RA,RB), so the address-mismatch and cross-function cases do not occur here. ABA-prone lock-free pops cannot be counted statically, so no FM2 bug is proven.

Clear the reservation on every stwcx. Keep the current fast CAS as the default for ports that do not need it. Also emit cr0.eq=0 when lwarx never executed in the function (statically visible), though that case never appears in FM2.
expected_gain: Correctness only. Expected cost is one extra cached load and one lock xadd per successful stwcx. (at most 691 static sites). Needed for ports whose lock-free code is ABA-sensitive; no evidence FM2 is affected.
risk: Xenia's own scheme only bumps the generation on stwcx., so plain stores still do not kill reservations. Performance of the shared table with false sharing (4-byte entries) is untested.

title: Inline tiny leaves at recompile time: elide blr-only callees, inline __savegprlr/__restgprlr helpers and other leaves of 12 instructions or fewer

The hook-override list must come from config so a PPC_FUNC override is never bypassed (grep found no hook on 82404EC0).

Code size grows by roughly 24k sites x about 5 stores or loads (estimate a few hundred KB), which could eat part of the gain through icache pressure, so A/B it.

title: Move the indirect-call table so the lookup displacement fits in int32 (saves lea, movabs, and a callee-saved register per function)
evidence: ppc_context.h:113 puts the table at 0x82B50000, so `base + TABLE - 2*CODE_BASE` = -2,173,108,224, which is 25.6 MB below INT32_MIN. clang therefore emits `movabs r14, -2173108224` plus `lea rax,[rdi+2*rax]; call qword ptr [r14+rax]` and spends r14 (push/pop) in every function with an indirect call (r0.asm: sub_821E0000). A scratch copy with the table at 0x84400000 (disp = -2,147,221,504, which fits) compiled one file (r0_tbl.asm): `call qword ptr [rdi + 2*rax - 2147221504]`. Measured on ppc_recomp.0.cpp: instructions 32,668 -> 32,014 (-654, -2.0%), `lea reg,[reg+2*reg]` 375 -> 0, `movabs r14` 13 -> 0, `push r14` 39 -> 18. Guest range 0x80000000-0xA0000000 is already committed RW in src\memory.cpp:138, and nothing is mapped at 0x843C0000-0x85400000, so it is free for the table. There are 22,473 indirect-call sites.
proposal: In ppc_context.h change PPC_LOOKUP_FUNC to `*(PPCFunc**)(x + TABLE_BASE - 2ull*PPC_CODE_BASE + uint64_t(uint32_t(y))*2)`, with TABLE_BASE a generated constant >= 2*CODE_BASE - 2^31 (0x843C0000 for FM2), and make the recompiler pick or validate it in ppc_config.h. Update the loader fill (src\loader.cpp:285) and wheel_ff.cpp:289, which use the same macro and so follow automatically. Have XenonRecomp emit a static_assert that the displacement fits in int32.
expected_gain: Estimate under 0.5% dynamic, from the 2% static instruction reduction in file 0 plus fewer push/pop pairs. Free for FX and iGPU CPUs. About 2 minutes of code, and it also reduces register pressure in indirect-call-heavy functions.
risk: Very low. The only hazard is a guest allocation overlapping 0x843C0000-0x85400000 (none seen in memory.cpp; the virtual heap is 0x40000000-0x7F000000).

verify.evidence_checked:
Re-derived in the shell. Current macro (out/ppc_tu4/ppc_context.h:113) puts the table at IMAGE_BASE+IMAGE_SIZE = 0x82B50000. The displacement 0x82B50000 - 2*0x821E0000 is -2,173,108,224, below INT32_MIN, so the claim holds. 22,473 PPC_CALL_INDIRECT_FUNC sites in out/ppc_tu4 (grep -o count), 388 in file 0.

I compiled a minimal snippet with clang++ -O2. The old macro gives `lea rax,[rdx+2*rax]; movabs r8,-2173108224; jmp [r8+rax]`. A table at 0x843C0000 gives `jmp [rdx+2*rax-2147483648]`, which is the same single-instruction form the finding describes. The finding's 0x843C0000 base yields exactly -2^31, which fits int32, so that floor is right. I did not recompile ppc_recomp.0.cpp, so the 32,668 -> 32,014 instruction counts and the push r14 counts are not independently reproduced. The snippet is consistent with them.

Memory: the new table would span 0x843C0000 to about 0x852F9E98 (2 x 0x79CF4C bytes). src/memory.cpp commits the whole 0x00000000-0xA0000000 range read-write apart from the writeback and MMIO window at 0x7F000000. The guest virtual heap is Init(0x40000000, 0x7F000000), so it never reaches 0x84xxxxxx. I found no other 0x84/0x85 guest ranges in src (grep). The only users of PPC_LOOKUP_FUNC are kernel/thread.cpp:276, kernel/wheel_ff.cpp:289 and loader.cpp:286, and all follow the macro. Nothing is parked or ruled out in the brief that covers this. It is not the r14-r31-as-locals idea, because the r14 it saves is the compiler's own spill of the movabs constant.

One unchecked side effect: the code changes, so the PGO profiles (build/pgo-gen, build/pgo-use) are stale until regenerated.

The finding's own 2.0% static instruction drop in file 0 is unverified. Direction is right: cheap, safe, slightly positive, and more useful on the FX, which has fewer registers to spare.

Before adopting it: (1) make the recompiler derive the table base and emit a static_assert that the displacement fits int32; (2) hardcode no gap after the image, and check that the xex's other modules or a larger title do not reach 0x843C0000; (3) refresh the PGO profile. title: Unmapped indirect-call targets crash with rip=0 and no diagnostic
evidence: PPC_CALL_INDIRECT_FUNC (ppc_context.h:116) is `(*(PPCFunc**)(table + off))(ctx, base)` with no null or range check. Only the host-side GuestCall (src\kernel\thread.cpp:276-279) checks `!func` and reports the guest address and LR. There are 22,473 inline sites (bctrl and tail bctr). The table is filled only for the 50,966 functions in PPCFuncMappings (loader.cpp:285), so a pointer to a mid-function address, an SEH funclet, or an address outside CODE_BASE..+CODE_SIZE (the index is unbounded and reads arbitrary guest memory as a function pointer) calls NULL or garbage.
proposal: At load, fill every table slot with a single stub `PPC_FUNC(ppc_unmapped)` that Fatal()s with ctx.lr (the call site, lr-4 is the bctrl) and the intended target. The target is not in ctx for local-ctr code, so also have the recompiler emit `ctx.ctr = ctr.u32` only on a slow-path: PPC_CALL_INDIRECT_FUNC(x) could become `(PPC_LOOKUP_FUNC(base,x) ?: ppc_unmapped_trampoline)`, but the slot-fill approach costs nothing at runtime. Fill is 2M x 8 B (about 16 MB), a few ms at startup.
expected_gain: No runtime gain; turns hard-to-debug AV-at-0 crashes into an actionable message (the PGR4 and FM2 ERROR-fragment bugs and the parked SEH funclet issue would be caught immediately).
risk: Page-touching 15.6 MB of table at startup (a few ms). Slots for hooks are overwritten after the fill, so keep the fill before the hook install.

There are 22,473 PPC_CALL_INDIRECT_FUNC sites in ppc_recomp.*.cpp (counted by grep). Generated code sets `ctx.lr = <next addr>` before each bctrl, so lr identifies the call site, but ctr is a local and the target is not in ctx. loader.cpp:285-286 fills only PPCFuncMappings, and GuestCall (thread.cpp:276-279) is the only place that checks for null. The table size is PPC_CODE_SIZE 0x79CF4C x 2, about 15.6 MB, so the size claim holds. I did not compile anything or measure the startup cost, so the "a few ms" figure is an unmeasured estimate. Three things weaken the finding. (1) crash.cpp:49-58 already logs the exception, the host and guest fault address, and the guest lr, r1 and r3 of the crashing thread. A null call is therefore already attributable to a call site, and the finding's claim of "no diagnostic" is overstated. What is missing is only the target address. (2) The slot fill does not cover addresses outside CODE_BASE..+CODE_SIZE. The index is `uint32_t(y) - 0x821E0000ull`, which wraps to a huge 64-bit offset and reads outside the table, so those still crash. Only unmapped addresses inside the code range are caught. (3) Filling every slot with a stub makes GuestCall's `!func` check always false, so that check would need a rewrite to compare against the stub.
verify.corrected_gain: No runtime gain. A small debuggability improvement: unmapped in-range targets fail with an immediate Fatal that names the call-site lr, instead of a rip=0 access violation that crash.cpp already attributes via the guest lr. The target address is still not available without extra code, and out-of-range indices are not covered. The claim that it would immediately catch the SEH funclet issue is unproven: the funclet problem is wrong register reads, not an unmapped call. Overall value is low to moderate.
verify.blockers: The hook-install ordering must be right (fill, then mappings, then hooks). GuestCall's null check must be updated to compare against the stub. The target address cannot be reported without a per-site ctr store (a runtime cost) or a lookup in the stub, and the stub cannot recover it from ctx. Out-of-range indices need a separate bounds check, which would add a cost at all 22,473 sites. The 15.6 MB page-touch at startup is a small cost on low-RAM machines and was not measured.

title: Many conditional branch/call forms hit `default: return false` and are silently dropped
evidence: recompiler.cpp handles only B, BL, BCTR, BCTRL, BDZ/BDNZ(+T/F), BEQ/BGE/BGT/BLE/BLT/BNE, their LR forms, BNECTR, BLR, BLRL (lines 597-750). The disassembler defines separate opcodes for BEQCTR, BLTCTR, BGECTR, BGTCTR, BLECTR (and CTRL variants), BNECTRL, BxxLRL (BEQLRL, BNELRL...), conditional-link BEQL/BNEL/BLTL/BGEL..., BSO/BNS/BUN/BNU and their LR/CTR forms, BNL/BNG, BTLR/BFLR/BTCTR/BFCTR, BDNZLR, BDZLRL, BDNZTLR, BDNZFLR (thirdparty opcode table, grep of PPC_INST_B*). Unhandled instructions fall to `default: return false` (line 2441); the file is still emitted with that instruction missing and only a stdout line `Unrecognized instruction`. Mnemonic histograms of FM2 (out\ppc_tu4) and PGR4 (out\ppc) show none of these forms present, so this is latent (bnectr appears once in each). Also BDZLR passes an extra unused format argument (line 659, harmless).
proposal: Replace the per-opcode cases with one generic bc/bclr/bcctr decoder driven by BO/BI: decrement-CTR, CR-bit test (including so/un), link bit. It emits `if (cond) { [ctx.lr=...;] goto/call/return }` using the same printFunctionCall/printConditionalBranch paths. Make an unrecognized opcode a hard generation error, not a warning.
expected_gain: No perf change. Closes a silent-miscompile class for future ports (cheap insurance: about 20 lines replaces about 40 cases).
risk: Low. Compare the regenerated FM2/PGR4 output byte-for-byte for the existing cases.

verify.evidence_checked: I re-read recompiler.cpp. The case list at lines 597-750 matches the claim: B, BL, BCTR, BCTRL, BDZ, BDZLR, BDNZ, BDNZT, BDNZF, the BEQ/BGE/BGT/BLE/BLT/BNE set and their LR forms, BNECTR, BLR and BLRL. There is no BEQCTR, BLTCTR, BEQLRL, BSO, BEQL or similar, and no BDZL, BDZT or BDZF. thirdparty/disasm/ppc-dis.c does define those opcodes, e.g. beql (line 2896), bso (2905), beqlrl (3173), and the 221 distinct PPC_INST_B* ids in that file are far more than the 25 handled. One addition the finding missed: BDNZF assumes the eq bit and ignores BI (comment says "assuming eq"), and BDNZT only handles lt/gt/eq/so. Both are latent bugs of the same class. I did not re-grep the mnemonic histograms of out\ppc_tu4 and out\ppc, so the "none present" claim is taken from the researcher. Latency is consistent with the generator never printing "Unrecognized".

Making the unrecognized-instruction case a hard error (nonzero exit when Recompile(fn) returns false) is the cheapest part and worth doing first.

The disassembler's operand layout differs per opcode, so the BI/BO fields must be re-extracted from the raw instruction word. Hint suffixes (+/-) must not change semantics.

title: Known FCTID/FCTIDZ saturation bug (listed for completeness; branch-free fix available)
evidence: Already identified by the user at recompiler.cpp ~910/915: a double of exactly 2^63 gives 0x8000000000000000 instead of saturating to 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF. This is outside the control-flow area, so it was not re-measured.
proposal: Emit a helper `ppc_fctid(double)` in ppc_context.h that returns INT64_MAX when `d >= 9223372036854775808.0` and INT64_MIN for NaN or `d < -2^63`, otherwise `_mm_cvttsd_si64`. Use it for both FCTID and FCTIDZ (the rounding mode is applied before the convert for FCTID).
expected_gain: Correctness only.
risk: Very low.

verify.evidence_checked: Re-read recompiler.cpp lines 912-920. FCTID (line 914) emits `(f.f64 > double(LLONG_MAX)) ? LLONG_MAX : simde_mm_cvtsd_si64(...)`. FCTIDZ (line 919) is the same with cvttsd_si64. double(LLONG_MAX) rounds to exactly 2^63, so `>` is false for d == 2^63. The x86 convert then returns the "integer indefinite" 0x8000000000000000 where PPC saturates to 0x7FFF.... The bug is real and limited to exactly 2^63. Values above it already saturate. +inf and NaN behave correctly. NaN, -inf and d < -2^63 all give 0x8000... on both x86 and PPC. Generated code in D:\fm2-port\out\ppc_tu4 has the same pattern at 652 sites (grep of `double(LLONG_MAX)`). 13 of those sites are FCTID (rounding-mode convert), so about 639 are FCTIDZ. The comparison is a plain ternary, not a branch-free sequence, but the fix is trivially cheap. I did not compile anything or measure it.
verify.corrected_gain: Correctness only, and narrow. It affects only inputs of exactly 2^63. Real-game impact is likely nil. The fix is a one-character change, `>` to `>=` in recompiler.cpp lines 914 and 919. No ppc_fctid helper is needed. FCTID must keep the MXCSR-rounding convert (cvtsd_si64). The proposal's wording suggests _mm_cvttsd_si64 for both, which would be wrong for FCTID. The "branch-free" claim is moot because the existing code is already a single ternary. The same boundary check could be reviewed for FCTIWZ (line 924, `> INT_MAX`). That one is already correct, because INT_MAX is exact in a double and 2147483648.0 > INT_MAX holds. FCTIW and FCTIWZ NaN behaviour (low word 0x80000000) matches x86. Regenerating output changes about 652 sites in FM2 (a rebuild of all 204 files, no semantic risk).
verify.blockers: None. Low priority because the gain is nil in practice. Do the one-character fix as part of any regeneration. Do not adopt the helper as proposed, because it mis-specifies FCTID rounding.

title: Branches that leave the function are silently turned into `return;` (dropped tail calls and switch cases)
evidence: recompiler.cpp printFunctionCall (~l.401-402) emits `// ERROR <addr>` when the target is not a known function start. Callers then add `return;`: PPC_INST_B (~l.370-378), printConditionalBranch (~l.416-424), and switch labels outside fn (~l.620-626, `return;`). Analyse() (l.96-256) only seeds new functions from `bl` targets (l.188: `PPC_OP_B && PPC_BL`), never from plain `b`/`bc`/switch targets. Counts in existing output: FM2 has 1 `// ERROR` site, sub_82771F08 in out/ppc_tu4/ppc_recomp.101.cpp:11607 (`b 0x82773580` becomes a bare return; 0x82773580 is a mid-function block of sub_82773570). My scan of FM2's image found 72 `bl` and 3 `b` that land in the middle of a different .pdata function. PGR4's committed out/ppc has 110 dropped `b`/`bc` sites (35 distinct targets, all in the middle of a .pdata function, e.g. 0x82799594 x21, 0x8276DAE0 x13) plus 31 `// ERROR: 0x..` switch cases outside the function (out/ppc/*.cpp, generated with the final pgr4.toml). The FM2 auction-house crash came from the same mechanism: three XTS functions (config comment) lost their shared epilogue because EH funclet pdata entries sit between the body and the epilogue, so the `b` to the epilogue became `return` with r1 un-popped. Those are the 3 entries 0x82789228, 0x827BD528 and 0x827C4928 in fm2_tu4.toml. Their size overrides also swallow the funclets' own pdata starts (0x827895CC, 0x82789628 and the like), because SymbolTable::find() returns the containing symbol and the pdata loop (l.143-147) skips any start already covered.
proposal: In ReXenon Analyse(), run discovery to a fixpoint. (1) Collect every b/bc/switch target outside [fn.base, fn.end). (2) If the target lies in no function, make it a function seed. (3) If it lies in the middle of another function, clone-inline the target's reachable blocks (they end in blr/b) into the source function as labels. Do not make it a call: with cr_as_local/ctr_as_local the live CR and CTR locals of the source function would be lost in a separate function, and a call also adds a return. (4) Make anything still unresolved a hard generation error, or emit `ppc_unresolved_branch(0xADDR)` that logs and aborts, never a bare return. (5) In the pdata loop, do not let a config size override hide a pdata start; instead merge the funclet range into the parent.
expected_gain: Removes the silent miscompile class. PGR4 has 110 dropped branch sites and 31 switch cases outside their function (counts); FM2 has 1 dropped site plus the 3 hand-sized XTS functions. Deletes the 4 'tail jump only' hand entries in pgr4.toml and about half of FM2's 31 hand entries. No fps change expected; the gain is correctness, and the next game's cold paths stop failing silently. The fix is partly proven by hand already (config sizes fixed the auction crash).
risk: Clone-inlining duplicates code (small: tail blocks are a few instructions) and can bloat if a target is a large shared region, so cap the clone size and fall back to a function seed. Needs a regeneration diff on FM2 and PGR4 to confirm only the dropped sites change.

verify.evidence_checked: Reproduced the core mechanism. recompiler.cpp:402 prints `// ERROR` when the target is not a function start. The callers add `return;` for plain `b` (~600-601) and for a conditional branch out of the function (printConditionalBranch 409-415). The switch case at 620-625 prints `// ERROR: 0x`, then a console message, then `return;`. FM2 has exactly 1 `// ERROR` site: out/ppc_tu4/ppc_recomp.101.cpp:11607, sub_82771F08, which is `b 0x82773580` turned into a bare `return;`. The config comment in fm2_tu4.toml lines 40-43 documents the XTS auction-house crash from the same mechanism, and lines 44, 51 and 52 hold the hand-sized entries 0x82789228, 0x827BD528 and 0x827C4928. In PGR4's out/ppc, `// ERROR <addr>` lines total 130. Top targets are 82799594 x21, 8276DAE0 x13, 82762C74 x8 and 8276202C x7. `// ERROR: 0x` switch cases total 31, which matches the claim. The claimed 110 dropped b/bc sites is plausible, since 130 non-switch lines may include `bl` calls (a dropped `bl` prints no `return;`). I did not verify the 35 distinct targets or the "mid-function" property for PGR4. I did not rescan the 72 `bl` and 3 `b` in FM2's image. 72 mid-function `bl` targets sit oddly beside only 1 ERROR site in FM2, so either the config splits resolve most of them or that number needs a recheck. The line citation for the `bl`-only seeding is off: recompiler.cpp:209 has `PPC_OP_B && PPC_BL`, not l.188. XenonAnalyse/function.cpp:79 also tests PPC_BL. The seeding conclusion looks right, but I did not trace Analyse() end to end.
verify.corrected_gain: Correctness only, with no fps change. The impact differs by game. FM2 has 1 live dropped site (sub_82771F08, a 4-byte SEH-funclet-style stub that is probably never executed) plus the 3 XTS hand-sized functions already fixed by config. PGR4 has about 100-130 dropped branch sites and 31 outside-function switch cases, so the fix matters most for PGR4 and for future games. The claim that it deletes about half of FM2's 31 hand entries is unmeasured. The clone-inline proposal is sound in principle, but a simpler 80% fix is hard-fail or `ppc_unresolved_branch` instead of a silent `return;`, plus letting a pdata start split or merge a config size override. Effort is M for the full clone-inline, S for the hard-error and logging part.
verify.blockers: The clone-inline cases need care. A target inside an SEH funclet region, a loop, or a tail block that itself branches back into the parent can pull in a large reachable set, so a size cap and fallback are required. A regeneration diff on FM2 and PGR4 is required to confirm only the dropped sites change. Merging funclet ranges into the parent interacts with the parked r14-r31-as-locals work, because funclets read the parent's registers. The PGR4 target counts and the 72/3 `bl`/`b` scan were not independently reproduced.

title: Zero-config function boundaries: use .pdata ExceptionFlag for EH data, jump-table targets and data-pointer seeds for sizing
evidence: FM2: 40,974 .pdata entries cover 7.40 MB of 7.91 MB of .text. 50,729 functions are emitted, so 9,762 (19%) come from Function::Analyze() on bl-targets and gaps, and most of those have 1-20 instructions (XenonAnalyse/function.cpp). Analyze() ends blocks at `b`/`blr`/`bctr` and knows nothing about switch tables. That is why the config has to say 'leaf functions without .pdata whose jump tables XenonAnalyse's size guess cut off' (fm2_tu4.toml l.38-39) and why `functions` has 28 entries in FM2 and 262 in PGR4 (35 'size to next .pdata', 85 split-at-call, 62+72+4+4 data-pointer/tail-jump/checked-iterator groups; pgr4.toml l.34-310). EH data is hand-skipped with `invalid_instructions` (3 values: 0x827745E0, 0x8296B6A8, 0x8277AEC0). But .pdata bit 31 (ExceptionFlag) marks exactly these: 404 FM2 functions have it, and the 8 bytes at begin-8 are (handler, scope table): 346x 0x827745E0, 54x 0x8296B6A8, 1x 0x8277AEC0, plus 3 flagged entries whose preceding words are code, not EH data. Function-start candidates reachable only through data pointers (virtual methods, thunks, callbacks): D:\PGR4-ReGPU\tools\datafuncs.py finds 84 new functions and 20 cut entries on PGR4. Run against FM2 it finds 20 candidates (most are SEH catch blocks) and 2 swallowed starts: 0x822AB818 (a 3-instruction `lis/ori/blr` returning 0x1C000, swallowed by config entry 0x822AB7A8 size 0x7C) and 0x8267A6C0. A call through such a pointer finds a null table slot and crashes. My gap scan of FM2's output found only 3 leftover non-EH code gaps, so the extents are almost right once hand-fixed.
proposal: Put discovery in XenonRecomp/Analyse (or a pre-pass in XenonAnalyse that writes the TOML). (a) Treat each .pdata entry with ExceptionFlag as owning an 8-byte EH header at begin-8 (drop `invalid_instructions`). (b) Run switch-table detection (finding 3) before sizing and feed each table's targets in as extra block roots, so Function::Analyze extends over them. (c) Size a non-pdata function as max(traced end, jump-table targets), clamped at the next known start. Known starts are .pdata begins, bl targets, data-pointer starts and the entry point. (d) Seed function starts from .rdata/.data words that point into .text and sit right after blr/padding/b (datafuncs.py rule), excluding EH scope-table catch targets, import thunks and jump-table labels. (e) Provide an `--emit-config` mode that writes whatever it inferred, so overrides stay diffable.
expected_gain: New game ports need no hand `functions` list. Today that is 28 entries (FM2) and 262 (PGR4) plus the datafuncs/missedswitch/switchfix scripts; PGR4 took 6 passes. Also removes the swallowed-function class (FM2: 2 starts). Estimate: FM3 starts clean versus the roughly 300 edits PGR4 needed.
risk: Data-pointer seeding has false positives (mid-function pointers from EH tables), which the 'after blr/padding/b' filter and the scope-table exclusion mitigate. Extra functions only cost compile time. Extending functions over switch targets could merge adjacent leaf functions, so clamp at the next known start.

verify.evidence_checked: I re-checked four claims in D:\fm2-port and D:\ReXenon. The first is the config's own comment at fm2_tu4.toml l.79-82: EH data before functions with ExceptionFlag set in .pdata is skipped by hand, 346 functions with 0x827745E0 and 54 with 0x8296B6A8, plus a third value 0x8277AEC0. This supports the claim that ExceptionFlag marks the same functions the hand list covers. The second is that the `functions` list in fm2_tu4.toml has exactly 28 entries. The third is that 0x822AB7A8 size 0x7C is present at l.59, and no sub_822AB818 symbol exists in out\ppc_tu4, which is consistent with that 3-instruction function being swallowed. The fourth is that D:\PGR4-ReGPU\tools\datafuncs.py exists. I did not recompute the 40,974 .pdata entries, the 9,762 analysis-derived functions, or the 404 flagged functions, and I did not run datafuncs.py on FM2. The recompiler already parses .pdata at recompiler.cpp l.177, but only XenonAnalyse's function discovery is at stake here.
verify.corrected_gain: The gain is for future ports (FM3, PGR4-style), not FM2 or PGR4 runtime. It saves hand-written config, which is real developer time. FM2 itself would fix only about 2 swallowed starts, and the 3 invalid_instructions entries are already handled by config. It does not improve speed. The "300 edits" estimate is an estimate. The effort is L, so by gain x confidence / effort this ranks low.
verify.blockers: Data-pointer seeding has false positives from EH scope-table targets and mid-function pointers. Merging functions over jump-table targets needs reliable switch detection first, and that is a separate finding. Without a validated before/after test on FM2 and PGR4 (the generated output must be identical or a strict superset), there is regression risk. Part (a), the ExceptionFlag header skip, is cheap and safe on its own. Parts (b) to (d) are speculative and unmeasured.

title: Switch-table detection: handle guard-less tables, use a CFG backward slice instead of a fixed 32-instruction window, validate against the enclosing function
evidence: XenonAnalyse/main.cpp ScanTable (l.~108-136) only scans back 32 instructions for the first BGT/BGTLR/BLE/BLELR and then a CMPLWI on the same CR. If none is found, `table.base` stays 0 and the table is dropped silently (the `if (table.base != 0)` at l.~234). The four patterns are rigid contiguous sequences (lis/addi/rlwinm/lwzx/mtctr/bctr and 3 variants) with no register consistency check. FM2's only manual table is the zlib inflate state machine: `lis; addi; rlwinm r0,r10,1; lhzx; lis; addi; add; mtctr` at 0x8281B51C (disassembled via build/tools/dis.exe) matches the pattern but has no local bound check, so it was added by hand. PGR4's first run logged 27 'Found a switch jump table ... with no switch table entry present' (out/recomp_first.log), fixed by tools/missedswitch.py, whose fallback counts words pointing within 0x2000 of the jump. `bge`/`blt`-style guards are ignored, and `labels.resize(imm+1)` would over-read by one for a `cmplwi r,N; bge` guard. When a bctr is not in the table file the recompiler emits an indirect call plus `return;` and prints a warning only if the previous word is 0x07008038 or a nop (recompiler.cpp ~l.2603). That produces a PPCIndirectMiss crash at runtime. The emitted switch has `default: __builtin_unreachable()` (l.632-634), so an undersized table is undefined behaviour. All 321 FM2 `switch` sites carry it.
proposal: Rewrite the detector in XenonAnalyse as a backward slice from every non-linked `bctr`: mtctr rX, then rX defined by lwzx/lhzx/lbzx (plus an optional add of a lis/addi base), then the table base from lis+addi/ori and the index scale from rlwinm/slwi. Find the bound from the dominating cmplwi/cmpwi plus branch of any polarity (bgt, ble, bge, blt, bne-to-default) using the function's block graph, not a linear window. With no bound, read entries while each is 4-aligned and inside the enclosing .pdata function (or the leaf's [begin, next start)) and stop at the first invalid one or the first non-monotonic data region. Cross-check the register against the cmp register. Report every unmatched `bctr` whose mtctr source is an indexed load, in an XenonAnalyse report. In the emitter, use `default: ppc_switch_miss(addr)` (a no-return diagnostic) instead of `__builtin_unreachable()`.
expected_gain: Removes FM2's manual inflate entry and PGR4's 27 missedswitch fixes (counts). Future games with other compiler orderings get an explicit warning instead of a silent tail-call. Does not change FM2 codegen performance, since the 320 recognised tables are already correct.
risk: A looser matcher can create false tables (a lis/addi plus an indexed load that is not a switch, e.g. 0x8276DE58/0x8276F398 which index a table of function pointers and tail-call). Require every entry to land on an instruction boundary inside the function, and emit a warning for anything accepted without a bound.

verify.evidence_checked: Re-checked in D:\ReXenon: ScanTable (XenonAnalyse/main.cpp ~l.104-130) only looks back 32 instructions for BGT/BGTLR/BLE/BLELR and then a CMPLWI on the same CR. If it finds neither, table.base stays 0 and the table is dropped (the `if (table.base != 0)` at ~l.234). The emitter has `default: __builtin_unreachable()` (recompiler.cpp l.632-634). The "no switch table entry present" warning exists at recompiler.cpp l.2602, gated on the previous word being 0x07008038 or a nop. The FM2 switch-table toml has 321 entries, and 0x8281B51C (the inflate table) is in it as a manual entry. PGR4's out/recomp_first.log contains exactly 27 "no switch table entry" lines. Facts hold up. Two weaknesses. (1) The `labels.resize(imm+1)` over-read for `bge` is hypothetical: bge is not matched at all today, so it cannot occur in the current code and only becomes a risk if the rewrite adds bge. (2) The finding is a robustness and diagnostics gain for new games. FM2 codegen and speed are unchanged. The PGR4 27 are already fixed by tools/missedswitch.py, so the benefit is saved manual work. I did not reproduce the generated-code or runtime PPCIndirectMiss claims. I did not verify the 0x8276DE58 and 0x8276F398 false-positive examples.
verify.corrected_gain: No speed gain for FM2. The value is correctness and tooling for new games: fewer manual switch-table entries and a loud diagnostic instead of a silent indirect-call miss. The cheap, high-confidence part is changing `__builtin_unreachable()` to a diagnostic no-return `ppc_switch_miss`, plus an XenonAnalyse report of unmatched bctr sites. That is S effort. The full CFG backward-slice rewrite is M effort and carries false-positive risk, so it is optional.
verify.blockers: Nothing disproves it. The full rewrite is unmeasured and risks false tables, so every table it accepts would need validation against the enclosing function. FM2 gets no benefit from it. The `bge` over-read is a hypothetical bug in the proposal, not an existing one. Nothing was run.

title: Unimplemented instructions are skipped silently; 91 of 239 vector mnemonics and ~35 scalar ones have no case; vpkd3d128 covers 3 of 7 pack types
evidence: recompiler.cpp: the `default: return false;` of the big switch (l.2441-2442) leads to a `fmt::println("Unrecognized instruction ...")` (l.2605-2608) but the function body continues with NO code for that instruction, and a comment line is the only trace. `__builtin_debugtrap()` is also emitted at l.2113 (vpkd3d128: only formats 0, 3, 5 are done) and l.2391 (vupkd3d128 unknown format). (3) Add the ~35 scalar ones (mechanical; model on ADDZE/ADDE and the existing update-form integer loads) and the VMX integer set using SIMDe, which is already vendored. (4) Complete vpkd3d128 to all 7 pack types following Xenia's emitters. (5) Add a `trap_mode` setting: log-and-continue for conditional divide-by-zero guards like `tdllei r9,0`, hard stop for `twi 31`.
expected_gain: Zero current fps effect. It prevents silently wrong code for FM3 and other ports; instead of hunting a hang, the build gives a complete list of missing opcodes up front (PGR4 hit 6 kinds on first run: lhbrx x18, lvehx x16, vnor x25, vcmpgtuw x4, vcfpuxws128 x2, vcmpbfp. x2). FM2's blrl fix is a certain correctness win in the auction/XTS path.
risk: Low. New instruction semantics need a unit test per opcode (XenonTests exists); VMX saturating ops are easy to get wrong without a reference such as Xenia's HIR tests. Failing the build on unimplemented opcodes needs an opt-out so unreachable library code does not block a port.

verify.evidence_checked: I reproduced these points in the source. (1) ReXenon recompiler.cpp has `default: return false;` at l.2441-2442. At l.2605-2608 that only prints "Unrecognized instruction" and sets allRecompiled=false. The result of Recompile(fn) is discarded at l.2791 and l.2675 only returns the flag. The function body is therefore emitted with nothing for that instruction, which is a silent skip. (2) `__builtin_debugtrap()` is emitted at l.2113 (vpkd3d128 default) and l.2391. (3) Spot-checked case labels: LFDU, STMW, ADDC, MCRF, FCTIW, LVEBX, VMAXSB and VPKUHUM each have 0 `PPC_INST_*:` cases, which matches the claim. recompiler.cpp has 347 `case PPC_INST_` labels in total. I did not recount the exact 91 and ~35 figures. (4) The twi, tdi, twlgei and twllei variants are no-ops at l.1762-1780. (5) fm2-port's out/ppc_tu4/ppc_recomp.102.cpp:9713 has `// blrl` followed by `__builtin_debugtrap();` right after `mtlr r3`. It is the only debugtrap in all of out/ppc_tu4. I did not verify that ReXenon l.612 and l.724-728 contain the blrl and switch u32 fixes. I did not re-check the claim that FM2 and PGR4 use none of the unhandled opcodes.
verify.corrected_gain: Correctness and robustness only, no fps effect. The one concrete FM2 win is the single blrl debugtrap site (sub_8277ACD0, Live title-services path), and that needs only a regenerate with ReXenon. The silent-skip, loud-failure and opcode-coverage work is future-port insurance, not a measured regression. Item (5), a trap_mode setting, is a design choice. It would make twi 31 a hard stop, while the 7,406 twi sites in FM2 stay no-ops.
verify.blockers: None for the finding itself. Effort is understated for the VMX saturating ops and for vpkd3d, which need per-opcode tests. Making unrecognised opcodes fail the build needs an opt-out so unreachable library code does not block a port. Changing twi to a real trap could break FM2, because the 7,406 sites include conditional guards that the game may never expect to fire.

title: SEH finally-funclet entries are exactly detectable (28 in FM2, 72 call sites), which unblocks r14-r31-as-locals without a dataflow pass
evidence: The parked item (keep r14-r31 as C locals) fails because funclets such as sub_8242A6DC, sub_824328FC and sub_82773570 read the parent's r14-r31. Structurally, in FM2 each of these is a function recompiled from a `bl` target that lies inside another function's .pdata range. Example: 0x8242A6B4 (the parent) contains a second prologue at 0x8242A6DC (`std r31,-8(r1); addi r31,r12,-320; std r27..; std r22..; stwu`) sharing the body at 0x8242A6F8 (`b 0x8242a6f8` at 0x8242A6D8), so it uses r22/r27 inherited from its caller. Counts from my scan (g.py): 28 non-pdata function starts inside a pdata range (28 in a.py and 35 overlapping function pairs in h.py), and 72 `bl` plus 3 `b` sites from other functions into the middle of a pdata function (excluding the 236 savegpr/restgpr/vmx helper entry points). There are no `bl` into the middle of the caller's own function. Callers are recoverable from the existing recompiled output (e.g. sub_8242A6DC(ctx, base) at out/ppc_tu4/ppc_recomp.42.cpp:46943).
proposal: In ReXenon, classify a funclet as: a function start created from a `bl`/`b` target inside another function's [begin, begin+len), excluding configured save/restore helpers. For every call site of a funclet, emit a flush of r14-r31 (and any local-cached LR/CR/CTR) to ctx before the call and a reload after. Only those ~72 sites in FM2 pay for it; everything else can hold r14-r31 in locals. Mark the funclet itself `ctx-only`. This replaces the 'read-before-write dataflow pass' parked earlier with a call-graph rule.
expected_gain: Unknown, and I did not measure it. This only removes the correctness blocker; the earlier skeptic result stays valid: benefit depends on how much register-in-memory traffic r14-r31 cause on the FX/5800H CPUs. Estimate only: r14-r31 are the callee-saved registers the compiler uses in most non-leaf functions, so the traffic is not negligible, but a build with `non_volatile_as_local=true` plus this rule must be A/B tested on the FX (needs owner permission to use).
risk: A funclet can also be entered via the EH unwinder through scope tables (the port does not implement C++ exception unwinding, only Lua setjmp/longjmp, so those paths are dead today). Missing one funclet call path would read stale registers; verify with a debug mode that compares ctx r14-r31 on funclet entry.

verify.evidence_checked: I confirmed the central mechanism in one example only. In out/ppc_tu4/ppc_recomp.42.cpp, sub_8242A6DC is called at line 46943 via `bl 0x8242a6dc` after `addi r12,r31,320`. Its body (line 47025) reads r22 and r27 without setting them (`cmplwi r22,0`, `lwz r3,1408(r27)`), so it takes live-in r22/r27 from its caller. Its prologue saves and restores r31/r27/r22 itself. So flushing r14-r31 to ctx before such a call site would be a sound fix for that funclet. I did not reproduce the counts of 28 funclets and 72 call sites, because I did not parse .pdata. I confirmed that `non_volatile_as_local` exists in recompiler_config.cpp:28 and defaults to false, so the rule would be new work. The finding is inconsistent: it says no `bl` goes into the middle of the caller's own function, but the example call site is inside the parent's body. The call-graph rule still works, since it keys on the call target. It does not cover three kinds of entry: indirect calls through ppc_func_mapping.cpp, `b` entries (3 claimed), and unwinder entry (dead in this port). A debug-mode check that compares ctx r14-r31 on funclet entry, as the finding itself proposes, would catch a missed entry.
verify.corrected_gain: Unmeasured. This removes a correctness blocker only and produces no speedup by itself. Any gain depends on an A/B test of non_volatile_as_local plus this rule, and that test would need the FX machine, which requires owner permission. Treat the "72 sites" as unverified and about the right order of magnitude.
verify.blockers: The funclet and call-site counts are not reproduced. There is no measured fps benefit of r14-r31-as-locals on the FX or the 5800H. Other parked blockers still apply: volatile guest loads/stores limit register caching, and any funclet entered by a path the scan misses reads stale registers. The effort is real (a pdata/range classifier plus flush and reload emission), and the finding does not show that the payoff justifies it.

title: Indirect-call miss and bad switch index are undiagnosable crashes in the default runtime (FM2 has no PPCIndirectMiss)
evidence: XenonUtils/ppc_context.h:110-113: PPC_CALL_INDIRECT_FUNC(x) is `(PPC_LOOKUP_FUNC(base, x))(ctx, base)`, so an address with no recompiled function jumps to a null slot. There are 22,473 indirect-call sites in FM2's out/ppc_tu4 (bctrl) plus 557 bctr tail calls. PGR4 added its own PPCIndirectMiss (D:\PGR4-ReGPU\src\crash.cpp:289, ppc_hooks.h:57-58) to turn this into a log; FM2 has no equivalent (grep of D:\fm2-port\src finds none). Missed function starts are exactly what finding 2 tries to prevent, and the fixes were found one crash at a time (PGR4's config comments reference crash.cpp PPCIndirectMiss repeatedly).
proposal: Ship the miss handler in ReXenon's runtime header: `#define PPC_CALL_INDIRECT_FUNC(x) do { auto f = PPC_LOOKUP_FUNC(base, x); if (__builtin_expect(!f, 0)) ppc_indirect_miss(ctx, x); else f(ctx, base); } while(0)` (the same macro the ports already override), logging the target, LR and the caller. Pair it with the switch-default diagnostic from finding 3. Gate the extra check with a define so release builds can drop it.
expected_gain: No fps change expected (one predictable not-null branch per indirect call; I did not measure it). Each missed-function bug becomes a one-line log with address and caller instead of a null-jump crash, which cut PGR4's iteration time. This benefits FM2 immediately.
risk: Negligible. The null-check adds a branch at 22k sites, so check the CPU cost on the FX before enabling by default.

verify.evidence_checked: Reproduced: the macro at thirdparty/XenonRecomp/XenonUtils/ppc_context.h:112-113 is #ifndef-guarded and does a bare null-slot call. FM2 src has no override and no PPCIndirectMiss. Grep of out/ppc_tu4 gives 22,473 PPC_CALL_INDIRECT_FUNC sites, matching the claim. PGR4 does have PPCIndirectMiss (crash.cpp:289, ppc_hooks.h:57-65). I did not compile or measure anything. Overstated part: "undiagnosable" is wrong for FM2. src/crash.cpp installs SetUnhandledExceptionFilter(OnCrash), which logs the fault, guest lr, r1/r3 and the object registers. It also logs a 24-frame host stack walk whose recompiled frames carry guest function names, so a null jump reports the calling function. What is genuinely missing is the target address, because ctr is a recompiled-code local (crash.cpp:58 says so). Also, kernel/thread.cpp GuestCall already null-checks with Fatal(). The finding's suggested macro compiles in principle, and the #ifndef guard means the ports can already do this without changing the recompiler core, so the ReXenon-side change is mostly a documented default. The finding counts bctr tail calls (557) separately; those are not covered by the macro at the sites I checked (recompiler.cpp:638/646/740), so check them before claiming coverage.
verify.corrected_gain: Diagnostics only, with no fps gain. The benefit is that a missed function start logs its target address, where today the log only names the caller. This is a convenience for FM2 and for player crash reports, not an undiagnosable-to-diagnosable change. The cost of the null check at 22k sites on the FX is unmeasured. It should be an opt-in define, off by default in release builds. Effort is S (a macro plus a small handler in ppc_hooks.h).
verify.blockers: No blocker to the idea. Downgrade the framing: FM2 already has a crash handler with a host stack that names guest callers, so the value is only the missing target address. The CPU cost of the added branch is unmeasured, especially on the FX. The handler must be noreturn and out-of-line to avoid code bloat across 22k call sites.

title: Mode-neutral FP ops should not touch the MXCSR denormal state (lfs/stfs/lfd/stfd/fmr/fneg/fabs/fctiwz/fctidz/fcfid/stfiwx)
evidence: recompiler.cpp:888-1035,1085-1117,1571-1610 call printSetFlushMode(false) for pure data-movement ops (FABS, FNEG, FNABS, FMR, LFD, LFDX, STFD, STFDX, STFIWX) and for conversions whose result does not depend on the denormal mode. Those are FCFID (int to double is never denormal), FCTIWZ and FCTIDZ (truncation sends a denormal to 0 either way), LFS/LFSX and STFS/STFSX. Counts in out\ppc_tu4, from the comment line before each FlushMode call: 757 of 1,911 Unconditional (real ldmxcsr) sites and 17,130 of 21,354 total sites are triggered by these ops. Top Unconditional triggers: lfs 526, stfs 105, lfd 72, stfd 14, lfsx 11, fneg 11, fmr 10, fabs 4. Typical pattern, ppc_recomp.100.cpp:72736: `// stfs f31,80(r1)` forces disableFlushModeUnconditional() between two VMX ops, then the next VMX op forces enableFlushModeUnconditional() again. Perl simulation (sim.pl) of the existing csrState logic over all 204 files reproduces the current counts (uncond 1909, cond 19441). If neutral ops leave the state unchanged: uncond 1909 -> 1079 (-43%), cond 19441 -> 8583 (-56%). Host asm of one 855-line function (f1.asm, compiled with the build's flags): each Unconditional site is mov csr/or/mov [ctx.csr]/mov [rsp]/ldmxcsr and each conditional site is mov/not/test/jne. Removing all 19 sites cut 1227 to 1062 instructions, about 8.7 per site.
proposal: In recompiler.cpp, stop calling printSetFlushMode for the neutral set above. Make LFS/LFSX and STFS/STFSX exact in either mode so they stay neutral. For lfs: `u=load; if (((u & 0x7F800000)==0) && (u & 0x7FFFFF)) f = ±double(int32(mant)) * 0x1p-149 (exact, and a normal double); else f = double(bitcast<float>(u))`. For stfs: `if (fabs(d) < 0x1p-126 && d != 0) bits = sign | cvtsd2si(d*0x1p149) (current rounding mode, correct for denormals and the 0x800000 min-normal carry); else cvtsd2ss`. Keep fcmpu, fsel, fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fmadd/frsp/fres/frsqrte/fsqrt and every VMX FP op as mode-requiring, because a denormal operand changes their result. Optional step 2: replace the 'reset to Unknown at every label' rule with a CFG meet over predecessors. In sim2.pl the checks currently come from 8,920 labels, 8,590 call returns and 1,931 function entries; this would drop the label share where all predecessors agree.
expected_gain: Static: -830 real ldmxcsr sites and -10.9k conditional checks, about 830*9 + 10.9k*5.5 = 67k fewer host instructions (estimate from the 8.7 instr/site average above). Dynamic gain is unmeasured. ldmxcsr is a multi-uop, partly serializing op, roughly 5-15 cycles by my estimate (not benchmarked here); it should matter most on the FX-8350 and 5800H iGPU class, and be invisible on a 5800X where the CP thread is the limit. Cheap way to get the real number: add a counter inside setcsr in a throwaway FM2_PERF build.
risk: The lfs/stfs slow paths must be bit-exact; unit-test against the current double(float) path with denormal and boundary inputs, run under both MXCSR modes. fctidz and fctiwz are exact only for the Z forms; keep FCTID and FCTIW mode-requiring if rounding mode is not nearest. Low overall.

verify.evidence_checked: Source: recompiler.cpp:423-434 matches the described csrState logic. LFD/LFDX/STFD/STFDX/STFIWX/LFS/LFSX/STFS/STFSX all call printSetFlushMode(false) (lines 1085-1116, 1570-1610). The ppc_recomp.100.cpp:72736 pattern (stfs f31 forcing disableFlushModeUnconditional between two VMX ops) reproduces exactly. The 'fmr' at 72729 shows the conditional form. Site counts in out/ppc_tu4: about 30.6k lfs, 21.6k stfs, 6.5k lfd, so the neutral ops are very frequent. I did not rerun the Perl sims or the asm. The semantics are sound for the pure-move ops (lfd/stfd/fmr/fneg/fabs/stfiwx/fcfid/fctiwz/fctidz): no arithmetic happens, so the mode is irrelevant. The proposed exact lfs/stfs slow paths are also correct (the power-of-2 scaling is exact; the min-normal carry is handled). One edge is not exact: with DAZ on, a double-denormal input to the stfs path would be treated as 0, whereas directed rounding on hardware would give the min float denormal. That is negligible. The main flaw is the gain accounting. The -10.9k conditional checks and the ~67k instruction saving ignore the code ADDED at the lfs/stfs sites. Only about 17k of the roughly 52k lfs/stfs sites currently emit a flush-mode call. Making them mode-neutral means every one of the 52k sites needs the exponent test (lfs) or abs-compare-and-branch (stfs), about 3-5 instructions each, on a path that is highly predictable today. That roughly cancels the 4-instruction conditional checks removed and likely grows code size. Only the removed unconditional ldmxcsr sites are a clear win.
verify.corrected_gain: Free, no added code: mode-neutral lfd/stfd/lfdx/stfdx/stfiwx/fmr/fneg/fabs/fnabs/fcfid/fctiwz/fctidz. From the author's own top-trigger list, only about 111 Unconditional sites (lfd 72, stfd 14, fneg 11, fmr 10, fabs 4) plus their conditional checks, a small static gain. The lfs/stfs part (526+105 Unconditional sites, the bulk of the claimed gain) costs extra instructions at about 52k sites, so net static instruction savings are near zero or negative. Any real gain depends on ldmxcsr being hot in dynamic execution, which is unmeasured. Treat it as an unmeasured micro-gain, and measure it with the proposed setcsr counter before implementing the lfs/stfs half.
verify.blockers: 1) The 67k-instruction saving ignores the code the lfs/stfs slow-path checks add at every lfs/stfs site, so the net static benefit is unproven. 2) There is no dynamic evidence (counter or benchmark) that ldmxcsr toggles around these ops are hot. 3) The lfs/stfs rewrite needs bit-exact tests across both MXCSR modes and all rounding modes (including the DAZ double-denormal edge). 4) The optional CFG-meet step 2 is unevaluated and would interact with SEH funclets and indirect-branch targets.

title: Unimplemented instructions are silently dropped: 91 VMX opcodes plus FP update-forms, fctiw, fcmpo, fnmadd, mtfsb*/mtfsfi/mcrfs, mtvscr/mfvscr
evidence: recompiler.cpp:2441-2442 `default: return false;` and 2605-2609 print 'Unrecognized instruction' to stdout and continue. Nothing is emitted for that instruction, so the generated function silently loses it. Diffing every PPC_INST_V/LV/STV id in thirdparty/disasm/ppc-inst.h (239) against `case` labels in recompiler.cpp (148) leaves 91 unhandled. They include vrlw/vrlw128/vrlb/vrlh, vpkuhum/vpkuwum (+128), vpkuhus/vpkuwus, vpkshss, vpkswus, vminsw/vmaxsb/vmaxuw/..., vrfip/vrfip128 (ceil), vsubuhs/vsubsbs/vsubshs/vsubuwm-family gaps, vcmpgtsw/sh/sb, vcmpequh, vmule*/vmulo*, vmsumshm/ubm, vmladduhm, vsum4*/vsumsws, vupkhpx/vupklpx, vsrh/vslh, vspltish, mtvscr/mfvscr, and the lvxl/stvxl/lvlxl/lvrxl 128 variants. FP gaps, by ids missing from the switch: FCTIW, FCMPO, FNMADD, LFDU/LFDUX/LFSU/LFSUX, STFDU/STFDUX/STFSU/STFSUX, MTFSB0/MTFSB1/MTFSFI/MCRFS. FM2 is unaffected: grep of out\ppc_tu4 finds zero occurrences of vrlw, vpkuhum, vrfip, lfdu, stfsu, fctiw, fcmpo, fnmadd, mtvscr and others. The PGR4 copy (thirdparty\XenonRecomp) still lacks 77 of the VMX ops. Also VCMPGTUB/VCMPGTUH (recompiler.cpp:1935-1941) ignore the record form: no CR6 update, unlike VCMPEQUB right above them.
proposal: (1) Make the default case fail loudly. Emit `PPC_UNIMPLEMENTED("vrlw", 0xADDR)` (a trap/log stub) and give the generator a non-zero exit code or a `--strict` flag, so a port cannot ship a function with holes. (2) Implement the missing VMX set with simde, using D:\xenia-src\src\xenia\cpu\ppc\ppc_emit_altivec.cc as the semantic reference. The vector registers use full byte reversal, so element-order cases like vpkuhum and vmule need care. Make the ~25 most common ones first: vrlw, vpkuhum/vpkuwum/vpkuhus/vpkuwus, vmin/vmax S/U B/H/W, vrfip, vsubs*, vcmpgts*, vcmpequh, vslh/vsrh, vmsumshm. (3) Add the CR6 record-form update to vcmpgtub/vcmpgtuh and any other compare that lacks it. (4) Add the missing FP update-form loads/stores and fctiw/fnmadd/fcmpo.
expected_gain: No FM2 fps gain. For a game-neutral fork this removes whole-function miscompiles in the next title; at present they show up only as one console line during generation.
risk: Low. Each new opcode is additive and can be diffed against Xenia's emitter; a unit test comparing simde output to a scalar reference (as in h1.cpp) catches element-order errors.

verify.evidence_checked:
I re-checked the key claims in D:\ReXenon\XenonRecomp\recompiler.cpp and in out\ppc_tu4. I did not recount the 91/148/239 opcode figures and did not compile anything.

- **Default case:** `default: return false;` is at recompiler.cpp:2441. The caller at 2605-2609 prints "Unrecognized instruction" and sets `allRecompiled = false`. Nothing is emitted for the instruction.
